_doc: Persona panel for the sim-to-real study. Demographics anchored to Pew Research (Holcomb, Gottfried, Mitchell 2013, 'News Use Across Social Media Platforms', n=5173 US adults) — the Upworthy-era audience. Cited as holcomb2013newsuse. Panel is FIXED and versioned for replicability; the same panel is applied to every package. NOT derived from internal product personas (authoring-bias control).

facts_used: ~half of Facebook and Twitter users get news there; Facebook is the largest news gateway
Twitter news consumers skew younger than Facebook
Facebook news consumers more likely female than YouTube/Twitter/LinkedIn
platform mix spans Facebook, Twitter, YouTube, with smaller LinkedIn/Reddit

personas.description: 29-year-old woman, scrolls Facebook on her phone during breaks; clicks human-interest and feel-good stories shared by friends; rarely seeks news directly.
24-year-old man, heavy Twitter user, follows journalists and culture accounts; clicks surprising or contrarian takes; low tolerance for clickbait he's seen before.
38-year-old working mother, checks Facebook in the evening; drawn to headlines about family, health, and local impact; shares uplifting or outrage-inducing stories.
41-year-old man, browses Reddit and Facebook; skeptical of sensational headlines, clicks when a headline promises concrete information or a strong narrative payoff.
57-year-old woman, mostly on Facebook; clicks emotionally resonant stories and anything about social causes she follows; less drawn to internet-slang headlines.
60-year-old man, reads news on Facebook and cable; clicks political and economic headlines, distrusts overtly hyped 'you won't believe' framing.
22-year-old college student, video-first, on YouTube and Instagram; clicks visually evocative or identity-relevant headlines; very sensitive to authenticity.
45-year-old man, casual Facebook user; clicks curiosity-gap headlines that promise a quick interesting fact, especially maps, lists, and 'what happened next' stories.
68-year-old retiree, active on Facebook with family; clicks heartwarming, nostalgic, or cause-driven stories; avoids headlines that feel like tricks.
34-year-old professional, follows news and advocacy on Twitter; clicks data-driven or justice-oriented angles; fatigued by repetitive viral formats.
